payload.name: Preserve Enumerated Items in Recommendations
payload.description: When a speaker recommends, offers, or lists concrete items (supplies, tools, ingredients, materials), extract each named item rather than summarizing them as a category.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly names multiple concrete items (e.g., acrylic paints, brushes, canvas/paper, palette) as recommended, offered, or needed, create the candidate content listing those exact items; do not replace the list with a generic label such as 'supplies' or 'gear'.
During CRUD, when merging or updating a memory that contains an itemized list, preserve every listed item; do not collapse specific items into a broader category unless new evidence contradicts them.
Capture only items explicitly stated in the message; stop after the stated list and do not infer additional materials.

solves: Extracted memories often paraphrase explicit enumerations (recommended supplies, ingredients, tools, or materials) into vague categories like 'supplies', losing specific facts that later questions need. This skill preserves each explicitly named item so future questions about the list can be answered from memory.
